decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Esther L. George.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that labor market conditions have improved further even as growth in economic activity appears to have slowed.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace despite the gl…”

changes.quote: Growth in household spending has moderated, although households' real income has risen at a solid rate and consumer sentiment remains high.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Since the beginning of the year, the housing sector has improved further but business fixed investment and net exports have been soft.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has been increasing at a moderate rate, and the housing sector has improved further; however, business fixed investment and net exports have …”

changes.quote: Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and falling prices of non-energy imports.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation picked up in recent months; however, it continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy pr…”

changes.quote: However, global economic and financial developments continue to pose risks.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to closely monitor inflation indicators and global economic and financial developments.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee continues to monitor inflation developments closely.”

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting further improvement in labor market conditions and a return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and falling prices of non-energy imports.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.22% APR costs about $50.92 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.87% and moved -7 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.58% would fall by about $11.76 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 195k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0.9% over the past year (March 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 98%, cut 0%, hike 2%.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
